title: Frames and circular structures
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches frame stories or circular structures specifically; the closest, Structure across a whole text, only mentions a text that ends where it began in passing and does not cover nested frames or the start-end comparison this point needs.

draft.title: Frames and circular structures
card: a story told inside another story. An outer story, such as a woman telling her grandson a tale by a fire, holds an inner story.
a text that ends where it began, with the same image, setting, line or situation. It is often a little changed by what came between.
Both create a link between the start and the end. Readers compare the two points and notice what has changed or stayed the same.
To evaluate them, ask what the link adds. It may suggest that nothing has changed, show growth, or make the inner story seem more believable or more personal.
draft.remember: Frames and circles link start and end, so readers compare the two.

a.q: What do a frame story and a circular structure have in common?
opts: Both link the start and the end for comparison
Both tell events in reverse order
Both use a narrator who is a character
Both end with a surprise the reader did not expect
a.why: Both set up a link between the opening and the close, so readers compare them. A circular text can be told in order, and neither structure needs a surprise ending.
a.clue: Think about what readers do when the end matches the start.

b.q: A short story opens with Jin sitting alone on a bus stop bench in the rain, bored and restless. After a journey of change, it ends with Jin on the same bench in the rain, calm and content. What is the effect of this structure?
opts: It shows how Jin has changed in the same setting
It proves that nothing in Jin's life has changed
It tells the story inside another narrator's story
It makes the ending a complete surprise to readers
b.why: The ending returns to the opening setting, so readers compare Jin's mood then and now and see the change. A circular structure does not always mean nothing changes, and there is no outer story here, so it is not a frame.
b.clue: The setting is the same. What is different about Jin?

a.best: Both link the start and the end for comparison

b.best: It shows how Jin has changed in the same setting
